Section 6 • \(P\)3D with the discrete Fourier transform

6.7 Ensemble expectation: aliasing, pixel window and discrete modes

For a homogeneous field on a periodic domain the DFT diagonalizes the covariance: the discrete counterpart of Eq. (5.18) is \begin{align} \Big\langle \widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}[\vec{p},q]\, \widetilde{\delta}_j^{(s)}[\vec{p}',q']^* \Big\rangle_{\rm ens} &= \frac{N^2}{V}\, \delta^{\rm K}_{\vec{p}\vec{p}'}\,\delta^{\rm K}_{qq'}\; P_{ij}^{\rm alias}[\vec{p},q], \notag\\ P_{ij}^{\rm alias}[\vec{p},q] &\equiv \sum_{\vec{a}\in\mathbb{Z}^2}\sum_{c\in\mathbb{Z}} P_{ij}\!\left(\vec{k}_\perp[\vec{p}]+2k_{\rm Ny,\perp}\vec{a},\,k_\parallel[q]+2k_{\rm Ny,\parallel}c\right), \tag{6.14} \end{align} so that \(\langle\widehat{P}_{ij}^{(s)}[\vec{p},q]\rangle_{\rm ens}=P_{ij}^{\rm alias}[\vec{p},q]\): the Dirac deltas become Kronecker deltas, and sampling the field at the grid points folds the power of all the modes beyond the Nyquist wavenumbers onto the grid modes (Poisson summation; Fig. 14).

Interactive

The aliasing is negligible when \(P_{ij}\) is small beyond \(k_{\rm Ny}\), i.e. when the pixels resolve the smallest structures of the field. For a non-periodic domain the Kronecker deltas are replaced by the window convolution of Eq. (5.21), evaluated at the grid modes and applied before the aliasing sum.

If each pixel stores the average of the field over the cell rather than its value at a point (e.g. the flux integrated over an observed pixel), each term of the aliasing sum is multiplied by the pixel window, \(P_{ij}(\vec{k})\to P_{ij}(\vec{k})\,|W_{\rm pix}(\vec{k})|^2\), with \(W_{\rm pix}=\mathrm{sinc}(k_\parallel d\Lambda/2)\) along the line of sight (and the analogous factor for each transverse direction, if applicable).

Estimator, mode counting and the zero mode.

The estimator is the average over realizations and over the modes in a bin, Eqs. (6.9) and (6.10). For Gaussian fields the modes are independent except for the pairs \((\vec{p},q),(-\vec{p},-q)\), so a bin with \(N_b\) modes contains \(\simeq N_b/2\) independent ones and \begin{equation} \frac{\mathrm{Var}\big[\widehat{P}_{ii}^{(s)}[b]\big]}{P_{ii}[b]^2} \simeq \frac{2}{N_b}, \tag{6.15} \end{equation} except for the self-conjugate modes, which are their own partners and have \(\mathrm{Var}=2P^2\). With a real FFT, each stored mode with \(0<q<N_\Lambda/2\) stands for itself and its conjugate partner and must be counted twice when averaging over a bin, while the self-conjugate planes \(q=0\) and \(q=N_\Lambda/2\) (the Nyquist plane, equivalent to \(-N_\Lambda/2\) modulo the grid) are counted once. Finally, if the fluctuations are built with the mean of the same sample, \(\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}[\vec{0},0]=0\) identically, and this mode must be excluded from the bins; if each sightline is normalized by its own mean, \(\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s),\rm 1D}[\vec{n};0]=0\) for every \(\vec{n}\), and hence \(\widetilde{\delta}_i^{(s)}[\vec{p},0]=0\) for all \(\vec{p}\): the whole \(k_\parallel=0\) plane is removed.
